current_events: Thirty people are killed and 47 people are injured in a drone strike on a cattle market in Nyala, South Darfur, Sudan

Brazilian environment minister João Paulo Capobianco reports that deforestation in Brazil's Amazon rainforest fell to 5,796 km2 (2,238 sq mi) in the year through July 2026, the lowest level since 1988 except for 2012

Australia agrees to provide Fiji with solar-, wind-, and wave-powered Bluebottle maritime drones and training for surveillance and efforts against drug trafficking and other transnational crime, with deployment expected in 2027

Hungarian prime minister Péter Magyar and Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskyy agree to improve bilateral relations during a meeting in Brussels, Belgium, with Hungary lifting objections to further European Union accession talks for Ukraine following progress on ethnic Hungarian minority rights in Ukraine
Hungary–Ukraine relations, Accession of Ukraine to the European Union
Cockroach Janta Party leader Abhijeet Dipke is detained in Delhi, India, ahead of the party's planned march

South African police rescue about 200 people from an unregistered rehabilitation centre in Mpumalanga and arrest two people while investigating alleged kidnapping and health and safety violations. Fourteen people receive medical treatment following the rescue
Czechs begin voting in the second round to elect 22 senators who were not elected in the first round

In women's rugby union, Canada defeats England 24–21 in a WXV Global Series match in Toronto, ending the Red Roses' four-year unbeaten run at 41 matches (the longest in rugby union history) after Shoshanah Seumanutafa scores a late try
